name: Enterprise ITAD upstream: EquipNet and CompuCycle corporate asset disposal and remarketing
region: United States / global (EquipNet North America; CompuCycle UK-headquartered, US operations)
notes: Recorded as the UPSTREAM of the used/ex-datacenter market and deliberately NOT priced. These are the refurb houses and IT asset disposition providers that take decommissioned corporate fleets and put them back into commerce; they are where ex-datacenter and ex-enterprise silicon physically enters the secondary channel. EQUIPNET: runs a timed-auction marketplace for ex-corporate IT with facets All Listings / Featured / New / Auction Listings, publishes Auction Terms & Conditions, and offers in-house Refurbishment & Repairs laboratory support plus IT Asset Disposal. It also runs certified-refurbished programmes (e.g. a certified-refurbished analytical-equipment project with a View Inventory link). Primarily laboratory and general IT - AI accelerators appear only opportunistically. No GPU lot with a visible price was retrievable without a session, hence price_usd null. COMPUCYCLE: enterprise ITAD - site carries IT Asset Disposal framed as 'secure and compliant disposal of corporate IT assets, with a focus on data security and environmental responsibility', plus a 'BID LOGIN' and 'Corporate Quote' motion and ITAD-adjacent asset-recovery services. No published price list exists because access is bid- and quote-only. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR ANY BUYER: the bid/quote-only access structure is itself the finding. Real ex-datacenter supply does not transact at published prices - it transacts through ITAD bid lots and one-off eBay pulls from liquidators. That is why the only defensible public price points for used accelerators are marketplace asks, and why those asks should be treated as ceilings.
